reasoning: Multiple credible sources from January-March 2026 indicate severe Iranian regime crisis: nationwide protests since December 2025, 2,400-30,000 deaths reported, currency collapse, economic hyperinflation, and weakened regional position. However, consensus analysis emphasizes regime resilience: entrenched IRGC control, 13+ million hardline supporters, no organized opposition capable of seizing power, and institutional continuity mechanisms. Sources note regime survived worse crises (2009, 2022). While some advocate for regime change, analysts assess collapse "absolutely improbable" without foreign military intervention. With only ~55 days remaining until April 30, 2026, and no imminent military action indicated, the threshold for regime fall (loss of de facto power over majority population, dissolution of core structures) appears unlikely despite unprecedented unrest.
